question: PSY-002 proposes signals for a coming regime shift. How often do rising variance and rising autocorrelation appear in a system that is not approaching any transition?
production_path: investigation: read PSY-002's six signals and recount the pinned quality trend with a blob-checked extract to see whether it varies at all
model: a noisy fold normal form driven toward its bifurcation (local AR(1) coefficient 0.5 to 0.9) and stationary AR(1) controls at 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9
estimator check: rolling variance and lag-1 autocorrelation against AR(1) theory on 200,000 points, one window and one Kendall tau computed by hand
simulation: 1,000 seeded runs per system at 100, 400 and 1,600 points with quarter and half windows, under a textbook, a fixed and a calibrated alarm threshold
adversarial: a linear twin without fold or drift, the same runs without detrending, a tipping positive control, nine one-line breakages of the script
test: byte-identical reruns on Windows and Linux, and five answered exercises checked number by number against results.json
hypothesis: In stationary AR(1) series, rolling variance and rolling lag-1 autocorrelation rise together often enough that the textbook trend test fires several times more often than its nominal 5%, and a rule held to 5% false alarms detects a real approach to a fold in fewer than half of 100-point records.
evidence: Synthetic fixture, 1,000 seeded runs per batch: in the stationary AR(1) controls both Kendall taus were positive in 334 to 461 of 1,000 runs, and the textbook significance test on the pair, nominally at most 5%, fired in 21.4% to 43.7% of them across three record lengths, two window fractions and three coefficients.

With the threshold calibrated to 5% false alarms on separate stationary runs, the joint rule detected the fold approach in 12.4% to 18.9% of runs at 100 points, 55.8% to 65.3% at 400 and 97.6% to 99.0% at 1,600, with realised false alarms of 3.1% to 8.0%; a fixed threshold of 0.5 gave 0.9% to 5.5% false alarms with quarter windows and 8.7% to 17.2% with half windows.

Estimator checks: on 200,000 AR(1) points the variance was within 0.21% of theory and the lag-1 autocorrelation within 0.0015 for the three coefficients, while 25-point windows read 0.555 on average for a true 0.9; a linear twin without fold or drift fired within 3.7 percentage points of the fold; results.json was byte-identical on two Windows runs and one Linux run.

Observed at Demerzel commit 4b03838800dcd4894f1e026461979bff1d985ca8: the quality trend holds 1,548 rows for 18 artifacts in 88 runs; compliance_rate and violation_count never change in 1,519 consecutive pairs, and citation_count changes 20 times, all on two runs. No indicator was computed on project data: the record can show neither signal, and its flatness is evidence neither for nor against an approaching shift.

The simulation covers one approach scenario, one noise level and AR(1) controls only, so the rates are not measurements or forecasts of the project. No human subject review, learner trial, translation or publication exists for PSY-012; research duration was not instrumented and duration_seconds=0 records that limitation.
